sections.title: Inside the 300kW Pilot Module
sections.body: Phase 1 of Kenya AI Compute is engineered to be a self-contained, high-performance ecosystem. This phase consists of two 40ft High-Cube modular containers, each delivering 150kW of net IT load. The primary focus is high-density GPU hosting, with each cabinet pre-configured to support 30kW+ loads. We utilize industrial-grade UPS systems with lithium-ion backup for instantaneous failover and N+1 precision cooling to maintain optimal operating temperatures. The network core for Phase 1 is built on a 100G Spine-Leaf architecture, ensuring that our initial GPU clusters have the high-bandwidth connectivity required for Render and io.net tasks. This phase is not just a test; it is a fully operational, high-yield infrastructure asset that establishes our technical standard for the 1MW expansion. Additional context: the project follows a clear rollout roadmap that aligns low-cost energy, infrastructure reliability, and flexible deployment models. sections.title: Technical Highlights (Phase 1)
items: Modules: 2x 40ft modular units with full environmental isolation.
Hardware: ~120 GPUs (training focus) and ~1,500 CPU cores.
Cooling: N+1 DX Precision Cooling with hot-aisle containment.
Networking: Dedicated 40G/100G uplinks for every compute node.
Uptime Target: 99.9% backed by captive generation and UPS redundancy.
